items.item: The form is split into titled sections (personal, job and contract, bank and tax, emergency contact, documents) in a single column, with a visible label above every field and no placeholder-only labels
items.evidence: Five titled sections (h2 '1. Thông tin cá nhân' ... '5. Giấy tờ') and every field has label.lbl above it, with placeholders only as examples. But fields sit in a 12-column grid (.grid-f with c3/c4/c5/c6 spans), so the screenshot shows three fields per row, not a single column.

items.item: Required fields are marked consistently, and optional fields are labelled as optional or left unmarked by a stated convention
items.evidence: Required labels carry '*' (span aria-hidden) plus aria-required. The header states '* Bắt buộc'. Optional fields (Quốc tịch, Nơi cấp, Chi nhánh, Mã số thuế...) are unmarked, which follows that stated convention.

items.item: Field widths match their content: dates, postal codes and tax codes are narrow; inputs use the right types (email, tel, date)
items.evidence: type=date on dob, idDate, startDate and cStart; type=email on #email; type=tel on #phone and the emergency-contact phone. Widths vary by content: phone c3, tax and BHXH c4, address c12, dependents c3. Dates are only c4, the same as first name, so they are not especially narrow. There is no postal code field.

items.item: An option to save the form as a draft is offered, and saving a draft does not demand every required field
items.evidence: Button #draft 'Lưu nháp'. Its click handler only calls setBusy, then sets the status 'Đã lưu nháp' and shows the toast 'Đã lưu nháp NV-0248'. It never calls validateAll.

items.item: Save and Cancel stay reachable while scrolling (a sticky bar or equivalent), Save is a verb label and is not disabled before submitting
items.evidence: Div 'sticky bottom-0 z-10' holds #cancel 'Hủy' and #save 'Tiếp nhận nhân viên'. The bar is visible in the first-viewport screenshot. Save is disabled only inside setBusy(true) after submit.

items.item: Fields validate on blur and on submit; with several errors a summary at the top links to each field and focus moves to the first invalid field
items.evidence: form 'focusout' listener calls setErr(el, check(el)). The submit handler runs validateAll(), then refreshSummary(). The summary appears at 3 or more errors, with links a[data-jump] that focus the field, and first.focus() is called on the first invalid field. The summary is in #summaryWrap at the top of the form.

items.item: Leaving the page with unsaved input triggers a warning
items.evidence: window 'beforeunload' sets e.returnValue when dirty. In-app links and Cancel go through guardedNav, which opens the #leaveDlg dialog 'Bạn có thay đổi chưa lưu. Rời trang mà không lưu?'.

items.item: The document upload states accepted file types and the size limit, lists chosen files with a remove button, and is keyboard operable
items.evidence: Text 'Định dạng PDF, JPG, PNG; tối đa 10 MB mỗi tệp'. input#fileIn is sr-only, which keeps it focusable, and is paired with label[for=fileIn] 'Tải giấy tờ lên' that has a focus-within style. The files table (#docTable) has a per-row button 'Xóa' with aria-label. Type and size are validated in the change handler.

items.item: Success is confirmed with a message that names the employee and is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: toast('Nhân viên NV-0248 ' + name + ' đã được tiếp nhận') on #toast, which has role=status. Caveat: the toast is toggled with the hidden attribute (display:none), so some screen readers may miss it. The persistent #status region is not used for the success message.

notes: Audit score 96. Its only violation is table-above-fold, which does not apply to a form page. Visually clean: white sidebar, blue-700 accent, 4 to 6px radii, no gradient or glass in the content, no emoji, no greeting header, no KPI tiles. The only gradient is the .skel shimmer in the loading skeleton, which is not a visual tell. The initials avatar 'LH' is for a person, so it is fine. The main failure is the three-column grid layout where the checklist asks for a single column. The summary only appears at 3 or more errors, which is a design choice and acceptable.
